header: HOW TO READ A WHEEL (RIM) MARKING: "8Jx20" -> rim 8 inches (203.2 mm) wide, flange contour J, one-piece drop-centre wheel ("x"), 20 inches across the bead seat. I read optional extras too: "ET35" (offset), "5x114.3" (bolt pattern), "CB67.1" (centre bore). Pure; nothing is stored or sent anywhere. The meanings are the standard ones (ISO 4000 / ETRTO / TRA wheel markings): the width is measured between the inner faces of the flanges, "x" is a one-piece drop-centre rim, "-" a multi-piece rim, the diameter is taken at the bead seat and is the number after the R of the tyre size. I treat the tyre widths that suit a rim width as a GENERAL GUIDE (about 225-255 mm for an 8-inch rim, 20 mm more or less for each inch of rim width); the tyre maker's approved rim-width range for the exact tyre, and the vehicle's manual, overrule it.

members.name: flange
doc: The flange contour letter(s); I keep "" when none was typed.

members.name: offset
doc: Offset ET in mm (positive, zero or negative); I set null when it was not typed.

members.name: pcd
doc: I keep the bolt pattern as the number of bolts and the diameter of their circle in mm.

symbols.name: parseRim
symbols.sig: export function parseRim(raw: string): RimSpec | null
doc: Reads a wheel marking ("8Jx20", "6.5J x 16 ET45", "alloy wheel size 7Jx17 5x114.3 CB67.1"). Returns null when the text is not one: I leave a bare "8x20" (no flange letter, no word like wheel or rim) alone.

members.name: tyre
members.type: { min: number; max: number; bestMin: number; bestMax: number }
doc: I give the tyre widths (mm) that suit this rim width, and the ones that sit best.

symbols.name: tyreWidthsFor
symbols.sig: export function tyreWidthsFor(rimWidth: number): { min: number; max: number; bestMin: number; bestMax: number }
symbols.returns: { min: number; max: number; bestMin: number; bestMax: number }
doc: Returns the tyre widths (mm) that generally suit a rim of this width: 225-255 for 8 inches, 20 mm more or less for each inch.

symbols.sig: export function rimWidthsFor(tyreWidth: number): { lo: number; hi: number }
doc: I work it the other way round here: the rim widths (inches, in halves) that generally suit a tyre of this width.

symbols.name: readRim
doc: Here I give what each part of the marking means, and what follows from it.

doc: Returns what a tyre asks of the wheel: its diameter, and the rim widths that generally suit it.

doc: These are the three figures, besides the size, that decide whether a wheel fits a car.

behaviours: 8Jx20 is read: 8 inches wide, flange J, one-piece drop-centre, 20 inches
the four parts, in order: width, flange profile, build, diameter
the width is 203.2 mm, measured between the inner faces of the flanges and not from the outer edges
J is the standard contour of modern cars, SUVs and crossovers
x is a one-piece drop-centre wheel (the tyre goes on and off without taking the wheel apart)
20 is the diameter across the bead seat, 508 mm, and the tyre must end R20
the tyre widths that suit an 8-inch rim are 225-255 mm, 235-245 mm sitting best
the notes say the maker's approved rim width decides, and that offset, bolt pattern and centre bore must match too
6.5J x 16 and 7j×17 (spaces, lower case, a multiplication sign) are read
offset, bolt pattern and centre bore are read when typed
JJ is a flange letter and 'ET 30' with a space is read
a bare 8x20 is left alone unless a word like wheel or rim comes with it
a dash stands for a multi-piece wheel
with every part typed there is a row for each: offset (positive pulls the wheel in), bolt pattern, centre bore
a negative offset pushes the wheel out, zero is on the centre line
a multi-piece marking says so, a missing flange letter is mentioned
ordinary text and tyre sizes are not wheel markings
a very long line is refused at once
20 mm of tyre width more or less for each inch of rim width
and the other way: 205 mm tyres suit rims of about 5.5 to 7 inches, 255 mm tyres 8 to 9.5
a tyre asks the wheel for its diameter and a range of widths
the three fit terms are explained: offset, bolt pattern, centre bore
